Enum Class LogAppender.AppenderType

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<LogAppender.AppenderType>
io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogAppender.AppenderType
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<LogAppender.AppenderType>, Constable
Enclosing interface:
LogAppender
@CaseChanging public static enum LogAppender.AppenderType extends Enum<LogAppender.AppenderType>
The buffer/locking strategy an appender uses. Unlike LogAppender.AppenderFlag exactly one is in effect for a given appender - set on the LogAppender.Builder (or via LogAppender.APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY) at construction time and fixed for the appender's lifetime; a publisher cannot change it afterward.

  • Enum Constant Details

    • REUSE_BUFFER

      public static final LogAppender.AppenderType REUSE_BUFFER
      The appender will create a single buffer that will be reused and will be protected by the appenders locking.

    • LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER

      public static final LogAppender.AppenderType LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER
      The appender will give each thread its own reusable buffer (a ThreadLocal) instead of allocating a new buffer per event. Encoding is done outside the appender's lock (the thread's buffer is only visited by that thread so no protection is needed while encoding) with the lock only held for the final write to the output.

      The same ThreadLocal buffer is used regardless of whether the calling thread is a platform or virtual thread. A virtual thread's entry becomes collectible once the thread itself terminates, and a typical unit of work (e.g. one HTTP request) logs several times on the same thread, so reusing the buffer across those calls still pays off even for short-lived virtual threads.

      This is the default type - see SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER for the alternative lock-kind opt-in.

    • SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER

      public static final LogAppender.AppenderType SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER
      Like LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER (a reused per-thread buffer, encoding done outside any lock) except the final write to the output is protected by a plain synchronized block (the JVM's intrinsic monitor) instead of a ReentrantLock.

      The Java language has no way to acquire a monitor in one method call and release it in another, so this appender's critical sections are written as literal synchronized blocks rather than going through a shared lock abstraction the way LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER does. LogAppender.AppenderFlag.REENTRY_DROP and LogAppender.AppenderFlag.REENTRY_LOG are still honored though - Thread.holdsLock(Object) is the synchronized equivalent of ReentrantLock's isHeldByCurrentThread(), so reentrancy is detected the same way.

      Motivated by Log4j2's own garbage-free appenders using synchronized rather than a java.util.concurrent lock around their buffer-transfer step, and confirmed by real-workload benchmarking to outperform ReentrantLock under platform-thread contention - this was the default for a time. Real-workload benchmarking under virtual threads found the opposite, a large and reproducible loss versus ReentrantLock for reasons not fully understood (classic JEP 491 pinning was checked and ruled out), so LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER is the default now and this type is an opt-in for platform-thread-heavy deployments that want the edge.

      Explicitly setting this type honors it even on a JDK where synchronized still pins the carrier platform thread when called from a virtual thread (before JEP 491, finalized in JDK 24) - the one exception is LogProperties#GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY: when that global property is active it downgrades even an explicit request for this type to LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER, since its whole point is a hard guarantee independent of anything else in the configuration.

    • LOCK_NEW_BUFFER

      public static final LogAppender.AppenderType LOCK_NEW_BUFFER
      Like LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER (encoding done outside the lock, the lock only guards the final write to the output) except the buffer is allocated fresh for every single event instead of being cached in a ThreadLocal.

      For deployments that want a hard guarantee of never using ThreadLocal anywhere in the logging path - REUSE_BUFFER is the existing no-ThreadLocal option, but it holds its lock across the entire encode-then-write critical section (the single shared buffer must stay protected for as long as anything is writing into it), so it pays for that guarantee with lock contention proportional to encoding cost, not just I/O cost. This type keeps LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER's low-contention shape (encode into a buffer nothing else can see, lock only for the write) while dropping the ThreadLocal - the buffer is simply a local variable, not cached anywhere, so nothing needs to be evicted or leaked-if-forgotten either. The tradeoff is a fresh buffer allocation (and whatever it grows to internally) on every single event instead of amortizing that allocation across a thread's whole lifetime.

      API Note
      not the default - LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER's reused buffer is the better choice unless avoiding ThreadLocal entirely is a hard requirement, not just a preference.

    • AUTO_DETECT

      public static final LogAppender.AppenderType AUTO_DETECT
      Picks whichever concrete type actually performs best for the platform this process is currently running on, decided once, at appender construction time, not re-checked afterward. Currently that means SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER when running as a GraalVM native image, or LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER otherwise - but that specific mapping is an implementation detail of this heuristic, not a contract. The whole point of this type is to track whichever choice is actually best, so which concrete type a given platform resolves to today may change in a future release without notice, as benchmarking improves or platforms evolve. If your deployment needs a specific type to always be used, pick that type explicitly instead of relying on what AUTO_DETECT happens to resolve to right now.

      Not the default - requires explicitly requesting this type, programmatically or via LogAppender.APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY. Downgraded the same as an explicit request for whichever type it currently resolves to would be: by LogProperties#GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY if it resolves to SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER, and by LogProperties#GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY either way.
